statements.t: “Commercially, we continue to be opportunistic on targeting price increases across the group, notably in Panama through Q3 and, more recently, in Jamaica.
We anticipate improving momentum in both revenue and Adjusted OIBDA in the fourth quarter as we move into the key holiday selling season and benefit from phasing of B2B.”
As is typical for us, we expect the bulk of our cash flow to land in the fourth quarter.”
We intend to stay disciplined and opportunistic as regards future share repurchases.”

Leverage – Our gross and net leverage ratios, each a non-GAAP measure, are defined as total debt (total principal amount of debt outstanding, including liabilities related to vendor financing, debt related to the Tower Transactions, other debt and finance lease obligations, net of projected derivative principal-related cash payments (receipts)) and net debt to annualized Adjusted OIBDA of the latest two quarters.
NPV – Represents the $250 million estimated pre-tax cash flow savings which we expect to generate over the life of the contract

As of September 30, 2026, we still have approximately 32,000 RGUs, which is composed of 16,000 broadband internet, 12,000 fixed-line telephony, and 4,000 video subscribers, that continue to be offline and are expected to be back online in the near term.

As a result of the impact of Hurricane Melissa, we incurred lower revenue during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and expect to incur lower revenue, for our Liberty Caribbean segment, during the remainder of 2026 relative to the 2025 pre-hurricane period.
In addition, we expect to continue to incur additional property and equipment additions as we restore damaged networks.
In August 2026, we entered into a strategic agreement with Amdocs associated with certain IT-related services intended to increase operational scale and business agility.
We expect this agreement will generally result in lower employee-related costs during the fourth quarter of 2026 and throughout 2027.

Programming and other direct costs of services include programming and copyright costs, interconnect and access costs, equipment costs, which primarily relate to costs of mobile handsets and other devices, project-related costs and other direct costs related to our operations.
We seek to maintain our debt at levels that are expected to provide for attractive equity returns without assuming undue risk.

With respect to the C&W and the Liberty Costa Rica borrowing groups, we do not anticipate any instances of non-compliance with respect to the debt covenants of these borrowing groups that would have a material adverse impact on our liquidity during the next 12 months.

With respect to our Liberty Puerto Rico borrowing group, within 12 months from the issuance of these condensed consolidated financial statements, in October 2027, the $1,161 million principal amount of the 2027 LPR Senior Secured Notes will be due and payable by LCPR Senior Secured Financing.

The proceeds of the 2027 LPR Senior Secured Notes were on-lent by LCPR Senior Secured Financing to certain entities within our Liberty Puerto Rico borrowing group, and the related senior secured proceeds loan will be due and payable at the same time that the 2027 LPR Senior Secured Notes become due and payable.

Based on the structure of our borrowing groups and the absence of any cross-default or cross-acceleration provisions between them, management does not expect such an outcome to impair Liberty Latin America’s ability to continue to operate or satisfy its obligations as they become due.
However, as our debt maturities grow in later years, we anticipate that we will seek to refinance or otherwise extend our debt maturities.
No assurance can be given that we will be able to complete refinancing transactions or otherwise extend our debt maturities.

In this regard, it is difficult to predict how political, economic and social conditions, sovereign debt concerns or any adverse regulatory developments will impact the credit and equity markets we access and our future financial position.
Historically, these arrangements have not resulted in our company making any material payments and we do not believe that they will result in material payments in the future.
In addition, we have commitments under (i) derivative instruments and (ii) defined benefit plans and similar agreements, pursuant to which we expect to make payments in future periods.
